family_comparisons.existing_scope: Two newly executed pre-registered discriminating tests against the pinned ZL3b corpus: (T2) a data-chosen byte-pair-merge re-segmentation test (hypothesis contributed by V. Gnuchev) showing the manuscript's H2|1 letter-pair anomaly is SEGMENTATION-DEPENDENT under a frozen decision rule -- at 40-60 symbol alphabets the gap to the lowest-entropy control language closes to 0.07-0.15 bits, with caveats that the crossover language (Greek) has an already-large raw alphabet (45 symbols), the gap against Latin/Finnish/Italian/English stays 0.2-0.6 bits at that size, and the association-merge criterion closes the gap less (0.21 bits); and (T1) the first executed illustration-linked-vocabulary test (editorial same-plant/similar-plant identifications vs text-sharing) across 12 same-plant and 28 similar-plant pairs with permutation and distance-matched nulls, found UNDERPOWERED because its own Culpeper positive control fails (p=0.44), with an exploratory size-corrected content-word lift statistic identified as the form that would give the test power.
family_comparisons.reason: Reuses T2's frozen 20-merge glyph-unit output only as a fixed input segmentation level; delivers a wholly new result set not part of T1/T2's scope or credited findings.

family_comparisons.existing_scope: A pre-registered, frozen-decision-rule adversarial audit of six prior generative-falsification family claims: (1) discovery and quantification that the shared corpus parser used by prior pilots leaves IVTFF markup inside ~24% of published types, requiring restatement of all headline manuscript metrics under a newly implemented clean parser (with two uncertain-space treatment variants); (2) an alphabet-confound test showing the H2|1 anomaly is robust to EVA multigraph/determinism-merge alphabet normalization but the final-glyph anomaly is alphabet-dependent (0.08-0.27 bit gap depending on glyph-identity assumptions); (3) five untuned cipher constructions applied to real Latin/Culpeper plaintexts, showing a plain verbose cipher of Latin reproduces both entropy residues and fails only a type-ratio gate calibrated to the contaminated parser count; (4) permutation-null and Currier-language/section confound analysis showing the 'neighbouring-page 2x sharing' and '30% page-private' structural claims are largely artefacts of language/section confounding and hapax richness; (5) a new medieval-orthography control (two Chaucer editions) testing whether the vocabulary-richness anomaly survives non-standardized spelling.
family_comparisons.reason: This submission's readability-hypothesis tests are entirely different questions and methods from the audit's parser/alphabet/cipher/confound structural findings; only shared clean-parser semantics are reused as infrastructure.

family_comparisons.existing_scope: A distinct generative-mechanism falsification pilot implementing Stolfi's published 2000 word grammar (core/mantle/crust unimodal-hill slot structure) as a template generator embedded in an entry/topic-carryover engine, and measuring two real-language positive controls (Culpeper's Complete Herbal 1653, Alice in Wonderland) with the identical metric suite against the pinned ZL3b corpus across 12 grid variants, showing (a) real language differs from the manuscript on conditional entropy, final-char entropy and entry-private vocabulary share, reframing prior 'unmatched by content-free generators' results away from a linguistic-content reading, and (b) the published grammar covers 86% of corpus word types with zero fitting and jointly reproduces vocabulary size, ttr, word length and page-sharing, leaving a residual mechanical-repetition signature (H2|1, final-char entropy, Zipf slope, entry-unique overshoot).
family_comparisons.reason: No shared generator, grammar, or metric; this submission tests interpretive content at specific manuscript loci rather than fitting a word-grammar template generator against corpus-wide statistics.
